name: LeetSwap WETH/BRIAN pair fee-transfer drain
summary: LeetSwapV2Pair exposed its fee-transfer helper publicly without caller, token, or amount authorization. An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.
notes: LeetSwap factory CREATE2 deployment of this immutable-bearing pair runtime. Archival code is absent in block 1967089 and hashes to 0x0f5ef9c858ac6a18a8ba1bec9eb648a6229cdf205a409108c6ace9e97f6bb85b at deployment and immediately before the incident; the pair has no proxy code-selection path.

The pair sent 11.360785525333188388 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 11.359785525333188388 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,862.36. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.
This pair-specific record is part of a coordinated same-attacker LeetSwap umbrella. Loss is partitioned by pair deployment and is not duplicated across sibling records.
